description: Caselaw benchmark queries from AR Video Review (April 16, 2026). Tests V1 and V2 query shapes against the same five Texas cases.

queries.label: Case Names Validation
queries.description: User provides case names only (no citation numbers). System must look up and validate each case, retrieving the correct case from CourtListener and binding the right citation number to each name.
queries.query:
Can you find and validate the Texas state cases? Trevino v. State
Formosa Plastics Corp. USA v. Presidio Engineers & Contractors, Inc.
Kroger Co. v. Persley
City of Keller v. Wilson
In re Halliburton Co.

judge_instructions.overview: The query provides five Texas case names. The system must retrieve the correct case for each name from CourtListener and produce a validation memo. The most critical check is that 'Trevino v. State' resolves to the Court of Criminal Appeals 1999 case (991 S.W.2d 849) — NOT any of the many district-level 'Trevino v. State' cases from other individuals. Additionally, verify that each case's inline citation number in the memo body maps to the correct case in the citations/sources list.

expected_cases.notes: CRITICAL: Must be the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals case, NOT any of the many district appellate 'Trevino v. State' cases (Bobby Trevino, Melissa Trevino, Abel Trevino, Jorge Trevino Cardenas, Joshua Lee Trevino, etc.). The correct case is about Rule 404(b) extraneous offense evidence and Batson challenges. If the citation linked is NOT 991 S.W.2d 849, this is a binding failure.

expected_cases.case_name: Formosa Plastics Corp. USA v. Presidio Engineers & Contractors, Inc.
expected_cases.notes: Texas Supreme Court case on fraudulent inducement / Economic Loss Rule. Citation number 960 S.W.2d 41 is the key identifier.
Premises liability / constructive notice case. Watch for wrong bindings: the known failure mode is binding 261 S.W.3d 316 to 'Glattly v. AirSera, LLC' instead of Kroger.
Texas Supreme Court legal sufficiency standard case. Watch for wrong binding to 'BMC Software Belgium, N.V. v. Marchand'.
Texas Supreme Court arbitration clause enforceability case. Watch for wrong binding to 'Reata Construction Corp. v. City of Denton'.

pass_criteria: All five cases are addressed in the analysis memo
Trevino v. State is identified with citation 991 S.W.2d 849 (Tex. Crim. App. 1999) — not a district-level Trevino individual
Formosa Plastics is identified with citation 960 S.W.2d 41
Kroger Co. v. Persley is identified with citation 261 S.W.3d 316
City of Keller v. Wilson is identified with citation 168 S.W.3d 802
In re Halliburton Co. is identified with citation 80 S.W.3d 566
At least 4 of the 5 cases have CourtListener URLs in the citations/sources list
No clearly wrong substitute cases appear (Glattly v. AirSera, BMC Software Belgium, Reata Construction) bound to the queried case names
fail_indicators: Trevino v. State is linked to a district appellate Trevino individual (Bobby, Melissa, Abel, Jorge, Joshua, etc.) rather than the 1999 CCA case
Citation 261 S.W.3d 316 is attributed to Glattly v. AirSera or any case other than Kroger Co. v. Persley
Citation 168 S.W.3d 802 is attributed to BMC Software Belgium or any case other than City of Keller v. Wilson
Citation 80 S.W.3d 566 is attributed to Reata Construction Corp. or any case other than In re Halliburton Co.
Fewer than 3 of the 5 expected cases appear in the analysis
Any expected case citation number is completely wrong (off by volume, reporter, or page)
judge_instructions.judge_notes: For citation binding, look at both (a) the citation number stated in the memo body next to each case name, and (b) the citations list document names vs. their context/URL. A case is 'correctly bound' if the case name in the memo body appears with the correct citation number. A case is 'in sources' if the citations list contains an entry whose document name matches the case name (fuzzy ok) and whose context contains the right reporter citation. If the analysis correctly discusses the holdings (e.g., Rule 404(b) for Trevino, Economic Loss Rule for Formosa) that is a positive signal even if citation numbers are slightly off.

queries.label: Citation Numbers Validation
queries.description: User provides reporter citation numbers only (no case names). System must look up each citation via CourtListener Citation Lookup and return the correct case name bound to each citation. This is the hardest binding test — known failure mode is returning wrong case names for 261 S.W.3d 316, 168 S.W.3d 802, and 80 S.W.3d 566.
queries.query: Please validate these citations 991 S.W.2d 849 (Tex. Crim. App. 1999), 960 S.W.2d 41 (Tex. 1998), 261 S.W.3d 316 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2008, no pet.), 168 S.W.3d 802 (Tex. 2005), 80 S.W.3d 566 (Tex. 2002)

judge_instructions.overview: The query provides five bare citation strings. The system must map each citation number to the correct case name. This is the primary binding test from the April 16 product review where 3 of 5 rows showed wrong case names. Pay close attention to whether 261 S.W.3d 316, 168 S.W.3d 802, and 80 S.W.3d 566 map to the correct cases or to the known wrong substitutes (Glattly, BMC Software, Reata Construction).

expected_cases.notes: This citation is fairly unique. Should resolve to Trevino v. State without ambiguity.

expected_cases.correct_case_name: Formosa Plastics Corp. USA v. Presidio Engineers & Contractors, Inc.
expected_cases.notes: Texas Supreme Court. Should resolve cleanly.
HIGHEST RISK ROW. Known failure: system returns Glattly v. AirSera instead of Kroger. If Glattly appears for this citation, that is a critical binding failure.

known_wrong_answers: BMC Software Belgium, N.V. v. Marchand
expected_cases.notes: HIGH RISK ROW. Known failure: system returns BMC Software Belgium instead of City of Keller. If BMC Software appears for this citation, that is a critical binding failure.

known_wrong_answers: Reata Construction Corp. v. City of Denton
expected_cases.notes: HIGH RISK ROW. Known failure: system returns Reata Construction instead of In re Halliburton. This wrong answer is non-deterministic — yesterday's run gave BMC Software, today's gave Reata. Any wrong case name here is a binding failure.

pass_criteria: 991 S.W.2d 849 is mapped to Trevino v. State (or close variant)
960 S.W.2d 41 is mapped to Formosa Plastics Corp. USA v. Presidio Engineers (or close variant)
261 S.W.3d 316 is mapped to Kroger Co. v. Persley (NOT Glattly v. AirSera or any other substitute)
168 S.W.3d 802 is mapped to City of Keller v. Wilson (NOT BMC Software Belgium or any other substitute)
80 S.W.3d 566 is mapped to In re Halliburton Co. (NOT Reata Construction Corp. or any other substitute)
All five citations are addressed in the validation output
The sources/citations list contains the correct case names for at least 4 of the 5 citations
fail_indicators: 261 S.W.3d 316 is mapped to Glattly v. AirSera, LLC or any case other than Kroger Co. v. Persley
168 S.W.3d 802 is mapped to BMC Software Belgium, N.V. v. Marchand or any case other than City of Keller v. Wilson
80 S.W.3d 566 is mapped to Reata Construction Corp. v. City of Denton or any case other than In re Halliburton Co.
Any citation is shown as 'Valid' but bound to the wrong case name
Two or more citations have wrong case name bindings

The sources panel contains primarily noise results (e.g., cases where 'S.W.' appears as a substring of a party name, like 'A.N.S.W.E.R. v. Norton') rather than real cases at the queried reporter positions
judge_instructions.judge_notes: For V2, the primary check is the citation-to-case-name mapping. Look at (a) the validation table or structured output in the analysis — what case name does the system assign to each citation number? (b) The citations list — do the document entries match the correct cases? A 'Valid' status on a row with the wrong case name is a double failure (wrong binding + misleading status). Also check whether the sources list is clean (real cases at those reporter positions) or polluted with S.W. substring noise from keyword search artifacts. The V2 query is a pure citation-number lookup that should use Citation Lookup API, not keyword search.
